title: Ethiopian Millet Porridge
community: Western and southern Ethiopia — the ancient small grain porridge
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Millet Porridge — finger millet (dagusa) flour cooked into a thick, slightly sour porridge in the Ethiopian genfo tradition, served with kibbeh and berbere. The western Ethiopian grain porridge — slightly earthier and more nutritious than teff, with a distinctive nutty flavour.
longDesc: Millet genfo is the western and southwestern Ethiopian answer to the highland barley genfo — finger millet (locally called dagusa or teff-like in some regions) grows where the rainfall is higher and the soil different from the teff highlands. The result is a slightly darker, earthier, extremely nutritious porridge.
steps: See ETH009 (Genfo) for the full technique.
Bring water to a boil. Add salt.
Add millet flour in a thin stream, whisking constantly.
Stir vigorously over medium heat 15—18 minutes until very stiff.
Mound in bowls. Well in the centre. Fill with kibbeh and berbere.
chefTips: Millet genfo is slightly more sticky than barley — stir with extra energy.
The result will be darker in colour than barley or corn genfo.
commonMistakes: Not stirring enough — millet sticks aggressively.
cookingScience: Finger millet has significantly more tannins than other grains — these polyphenol compounds give millet its characteristic slightly astringent taste and its dark colour. The tannins also have significant antioxidant properties.
sustainabilityTips: Finger millet is exceptionally drought-resistant and requires minimal inputs.
healthBenefits: Finger millet has exceptional calcium content.
culturalNote: Millet genfo is the porridge of the Ethiopian highlands' western fringe — where the landscape transitions from the highlands to the Great Rift Valley, where the cultures blend, and where finger millet has been cultivated for longer than any other grain in the region.
